reports.title: Report of Foreign Private Issuer Pursuant to Rule 13a-16 or 15d-16 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934

desk.headline: Net income up 39% to a record $1.09bn; IFRS revenue $5.82bn, a little below estimates; no formal guidance
results: Net income rose 39% to a record $1.09bn from $783m a year earlier.
Revenue was $5.82bn under IFRS accounting, or $6.26bn (+45%) on the company's own 'managerial' basis, which reclassifies some items and grosses up for tax.
Lending drove growth: credit income rose 52% to $3.80bn and fee income 51% to $913m, while funding costs rose only 19%.
Credit losses climbed faster than revenue: cost of credit was up 73% to $1.79bn.
Operating costs rose 47% to $846m, with marketing spend roughly doubling to $116m.

guidance.summary: Nu gives no formal revenue or profit guidance and the filing contains no outlook. On the call, as reported, management said its 2026 efficiency ratio should land at 19–19.5% (better than the roughly 20% it had indicated), rising in Q4 as delayed spending lands, and gave no 2027 loan-growth or margin guidance.

points: Customers reached 143 million, with record activity in Brazil; Mexico (16.6m) and Colombia (6.1m) kept growing quickly.
Late payments (90+ days) rose to 7.3% of loans, which management put down mainly to more interest-earning card balances; a $53m one-off hit came from Brazilian payment firms put into liquidation.
Net interest margin edged up to 22.5% and deposit costs fell further relative to Brazil's benchmark rate.
The new US and global accounts launched in Sep–Oct; spending there will be scaled only as products prove themselves.
Management said Nu is generating a lot of capital; an Investor Day is set for 8 December.
